source.title: CCML: A Novel Collaborative Learning Model for Classification of Remote Sensing Images with Noisy Multi-Labels
source.authors: A. Aksoy; Mahdyar Ravanbakhsh; Tristan Kreuziger; B. Demir

page_placements.theme: Held-out degradation without an established interpolation result

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests performance under synthetic multi-label noise using a different task and measures test-set classification scores; it does not measure whether the networks fit noisy training labels.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results on RS classification with synthetic label flips. Its own results do not report training error, zero training error, chance-level test error, unstructured inputs, regularization removal, or learning order. Cited results about memorization are not this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study motivates noise mitigation using networks' ability to overfit noisy labels, but evaluates held-out classification performance rather than memorization. It reports no training-set fit, optimization comparison, or learning trajectory. Its test-set scores alone do not establish V4's combination of perfect training fit and degradation toward chance.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: RCML improves robustness relative to comparison methods at high injected multi-label noise rates, with comparable performance at low rates. The authors restrict their demonstrated effectiveness to the tested deterministic-noise settings and note that accurate noise-rate estimation improves RCML performance.
record.recipe_differences: Uses multi-label RS datasets, synthetic binary label flips, and test-set mAP/F1 scores to evaluate noise-robust classifiers; it does not reproduce the original random-label memorization experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary with dataset, injected noise rate, class sample counts, and the estimated noise rate used to set the swap rate.

fits_no_version.finding: For ImageNet-pretrained ResNet50 with BCE on multi-label UCMerced, test mAP macro decreases from 89.5% at 10% injected noise to 74.5% at 40%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Synthetic multi-label corruption can reduce held-out classification performance; this does not by itself demonstrate memorization of corrupted labels.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems
record.problems: The paper reports classification scores averaged over three runs but gives no uncertainty values in the supplied text. Its noise injection flips a fraction of multi-label entries and reaches at most 50%; it does not report training-set error, so its results cannot establish memorization of random labels.
record.rows_left_out: Other reported method, dataset, noise-rate, and metric results are not extracted because the text does not provide their individual table values, and the stated UCMerced BCE scores are the available outcomes directly relevant to V4. Class-based plot results are described qualitatively but do not report the claimed training-fit behavior.

untested.parts: Fitting completely random labels to zero or near-zero training error, chance test performance, and retaining the original architecture and hyperparameters.
Relative training time and convergence speed for true versus random labels and across corruption fractions.
Zero training error on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.

Perfect training fit throughout increasing corruption and steady test-error degradation toward chance. Held-out mAP/F1 under 0–50% synthetic multi-label noise does not establish this combined behavior.
Whether explicit regularizers prevent fitting random labels and whether removing them harms generalization on true labels.
Learning shared real-data patterns before memorizing noise, assessed through training trajectories.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the record's V4 limits_scope verdict: missing training-fit evidence is an untested component, not evidence of a scope limitation. Table bodies are absent from the supplied text, but both extracted BCE scores appear explicitly in Section V-C.

versions.untested_parts: No completely random labeling condition, training-error result, or test-error-at-chance result.
No comparison of training time or convergence speed across label-noise rates.
No shuffled-pixel, permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise input condition.

The study evaluates test-set performance under synthetic label noise, but does not report training-set fit or test error approaching chance; noise rates range from 0% to 50%, not all labels randomized.
No test of whether weight decay, dropout, or augmentation prevent fitting random labels, or whether removing them harms clean-label generalization.
No analysis of learning order or comparison of real-label and random-label learning over training.

relation.reason: The method excludes suspected noisy samples to prevent overfitting, but its held-out mAP and F1 results do not establish any claim version.

tranche.reason: Uses susceptibility to noisy-label overfitting to motivate noise mitigation and reports classification performance. It does not measure training-set memorization, optimization speed, or learning trajectories.

source_check.notes: The supplied text is the revised RCML journal article, titled Multi-Label Noise Robust Collaborative Learning for Remote Sensing Image Classification; the pack uses the earlier CCML title. The reported test scores establish neither perfect training fit nor degradation toward chance.
